newsitem.title: CANADA: UGG sees W. Canada grains losing acres to oilseeds.
newsitem.headline: UGG sees W. Canada grains losing acres to oilseeds.

text.p: United Grain Growers continued to forecast less acres to be seeded to cereals this spring than last year in western Canada while oilseed and specialty crop acres were seen expanding.
But UGG sees wheat acres to expand to 27.73 million from its April 1 forecast of 27.393 million. The number is down 8.9 percent from Statistics Canada's 1996/97 estimate of 31.085 million acres.

"People are shifting away from wheat because farmers are carrying more inventories into the new crop year, so if you've got it in your bin, why grow it in your fields," UGG analyst Mike Jubinville said.
The Canadian Wheat Board said in March it was 1.5 million tonnes behind in its exports due to backlogs at Pacific ports.

All wheat output was estimated at 26.4 million tonnes assuming an average yield at 35.4 bushels an acres, up from 26.13 in April's estimate but down from StatsCan's 1996/97 estimate of 29.47 million tonnes on average yields of 35.7.
UGG elevator managers surveyed farmers June 2-4.
Canola acreage in western Canada this year was projected at 12.4 million acres, up from UGG's April estimate of 12.166 million acres and well above StatsCan's 1996/97 figure of 8.802 million.
Trade forecasts had set canola area at 12.5 to 13 million.
"Our seed sales makes it look like it might be a bigger crop and our sulphur sales are as high as when we had a record 14.3 million acre crop," Jubinville said.
Alberta's Peace River Valley seeding has been stalled by rain.
"Alberta's Peace River is seeding more shorter-season Polish varieties and some acres aren't being seeded," Jubinville said.

Canola output was estimated at 6.555 million tonnes assuming an average yield at 23.5 bushels per acre, up from 6.444 in April's estimate and up from StatsCan's 1996/97 estimate of 4.99 million tonnes on average yields of 25.7 bu/ac.
Barley area in western Canada was seen at 12.208 million acres versus 11.01 million acres in April but down from StatsCan's 1996/97 estimate of 12.40 million acres.
"Barley's higher than expected but given seeding delays in some parts of the Prairies, a lot of people are going on malt varieties as one of the higher-priced commodities," Jubinville said.
Barley has a shorter growing season than wheat.

Barley output was tabbed at 14.73 million tonnes assuming an average yield at 58.3 bushels an acre, up from 14.3 million in UGG's April estimate but below StatsCan's 1996/97 estimate of 14.995 million tonnes on average yields of 60.2 bushels.
Oat area in western Canada this year was seen at 4.384 million acres, below April's estimate of 4.529 million and down from StatsCan's 1996/97 estimate of 4.785 million acres.

Oats output was seen at 3.785 million tonnes assuming average yield at 66.9 bushels/acre, down from 3.921 million in April's estimate and down from StatsCan's 1996/97 estimate of 4.11 million tonnes on average yields of 68.4 bushels.
Flax area on the Prairies was forecast at 2.344 million acres, up from 2.098 million acres in the April estimate and 57 percent above the 1.490 million acres in 1996/97.

"We could see an all-time record production in flax this year. Farmers saw C$9 a bushel last harvest. Every five to seven years we see C$9 flax and the next year farmers go crazy and kill the market for the next two years," Jubinville said.

Flax output was forecast at 1.327 million tonnes assuming an average yield at 22.5 bushels an acre, up from 1.189 in April's estimate but down from StatsCan's 1996/97 estimate of 843,000 tonnes on average yields of 23.4 bu/ac.
Acres devoted to specialty crops in western Canada were seen at 3.753 million, down from April's estimate of 3.987 million but up from StatsCan's 1996/97 figure of 3.391 million acres.
((Gilbert Le Gras, Winnipeg Reuters bureau 204 947 3548))
